SOCIAL STUDIES — TERMLY EXAM #10 (TERM 1)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SOCIAL STUDIES
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which direction is Nakuru from Nairobi? (1 mark)
   A. East
   B. North-west
   C. South
   D. South-east

2. What does a compass needle point to? (1 mark)
   A. South
   B. North
   C. The nearest town
   D. The sun

3. What does the letter E stand for on a compass rose? (1 mark)
   A. Earth
   B. Edge
   C. Equator
   D. East

4. Which is the smallest county in Kenya by area? (1 mark)
   A. Kitui
   B. Mombasa
   C. Turkana
   D. Narok

5. What is the best way to compare the sizes of two counties on maps? (1 mark)
   A. Use the same scale and compare the areas
   B. Compare the length of the names
   C. Count the number of towns only
   D. Guess without a map

6. Which imaginary line crosses Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. The boundary
   B. The river line
   C. The equator
   D. The railway line

7. Which is the longest river inside Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. Tana River
   B. Yala River
   C. Nzoia River
   D. Athi River

8. Which physical feature is best for building roads, towns and farms easily? (1 mark)
   A. A plain
   B. A deep valley
   C. A steep mountain
   D. A waterfall

9. Which is the highest mountain in Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. Mount Elgon
   B. Aberdare Range
   C. Mount Kenya
   D. Ngong Hills

10. If there is no pavement, which side of the road should a pedestrian walk on? (1 mark)
   A. The side with traffic behind
   B. The side facing the oncoming traffic
   C. In the middle of the road
   D. On the side where there is no light

11. What is weather? (1 mark)
   A. How the air is on a particular day
   B. The number of months in a year
   C. The size of a county
   D. The height of a mountain

12. Which season is best for planting most crops? (1 mark)
   A. Cold season
   B. Dry season
   C. Rainy season
   D. Hot season

13. Which of these actions helps to conserve a historic place? (1 mark)
   A. Reporting anyone who damages it
   B. Breaking off small pieces
   C. Leaving litter
   D. Climbing on old walls

14. Which is a very old town on the Kenyan coast with narrow streets and stone houses? (1 mark)
   A. Thimlich Ohinga
   B. Nakuru
   C. Eldoret
   D. Lamu Old Town

15. What is a monument? (1 mark)
   A. A river
   B. A structure built to remember a person or event
   C. A bus
   D. A market

16. A tailor makes uniforms and a farmer buys them. What does the tailor need from the farmer? (1 mark)
   A. Food or money from selling food
   B. Nothing at all
   C. Cloth from the moon
   D. A tractor for sewing

17. Why can no person do every job alone? (1 mark)
   A. People are lazy
   B. There are too many skills and jobs to learn
   C. Jobs are not important
   D. Money is not needed

18. Which type of area in Kenya usually has few people for its size? (1 mark)
   A. Highlands around Mount Kenya
   B. Big cities
   C. Dry areas in the far north
   D. Busy lakeshores

19. Which pattern describes each family living far from the next on its own land? (1 mark)
   A. Linear
   B. Scattered
   C. Crowded
   D. Clustered

20. Which is the best way to show population on a map using dots? (1 mark)
   A. Draw a river
   B. Write the county name only
   C. Colour the whole map blue
   D. Draw dots where people live and give a key for what a dot means

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Name two historic places in Kenya and the town or county where each is found. (2 marks)

22. List four ways of caring for rivers and lakes. (4 marks)

23. Explain what neighbouring counties are. (2 marks)

24. Explain how a farmer and a trader depend on each other. (3 marks)

25. Give two reasons why farmers plant crops at the start of the rainy season. (2 marks)

26. Describe three problems that crowded areas can have and one way of reducing each. (5 marks)

27. Explain what may happen if people cut down all the trees on a mountain. (3 marks)

28. Explain two ways of showing appreciation to people who help us. (2 marks)

29. Write a short note to invite a resource person to talk about a historic place in your county. Include the reason and the date. (5 marks)

30. Give two reasons why some areas are densely populated. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
SOCIAL STUDIES — TERMLY EXAM #10 (TERM 1) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — North-west
   Nakuru is north-west of Nairobi.

2. B — North
   A magnetic compass needle always turns to point north.

3. D — East
   E is the short form of east.

4. B — Mombasa
   Mombasa covers the smallest area of all the counties.

5. A — Use the same scale and compare the areas
   To compare fairly we use maps drawn to the same scale.

6. C — The equator
   The equator crosses the middle of Kenya.

7. A — Tana River
   The Tana River is the longest river in Kenya.

8. A — A plain
   Flat land is easy to build on and farm.

9. C — Mount Kenya
   Mount Kenya is the highest mountain in Kenya.

10. B — The side facing the oncoming traffic
   Facing traffic lets you see vehicles coming towards you.

11. A — How the air is on a particular day
   Weather describes sun, rain, wind and temperature at a given time.

12. C — Rainy season
   Seeds need rain water to germinate and grow.

13. A — Reporting anyone who damages it
   Reporting damage helps protect the place.

14. D — Lamu Old Town
   Lamu Old Town is one of the oldest towns on the coast.

15. B — A structure built to remember a person or event
   Monuments remind people of important people or events.

16. A — Food or money from selling food
   The tailor depends on the farmer for food.

17. B — There are too many skills and jobs to learn
   Nobody can grow all food, teach, heal and build alone.

18. C — Dry areas in the far north
   Dry northern areas are sparsely populated.

19. B — Scattered
   Scattered means spread widely apart.

20. D — Draw dots where people live and give a key for what a dot means
   A dot map needs a clear key.

SECTION B
----
21. (2 marks)
   Answer: Fort Jesus in Mombasa and Thimlich Ohinga in Migori County. Accept Lamu Old Town or Gede Ruins.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct place with its location.

22. (4 marks)
   Answer: Do not throw rubbish into them, plant trees on the banks, do not wash or farm too close to the water, and tell adults about pollution.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct way.

23. (2 marks)
   Answer: Neighbouring counties are counties that share a boundary with your county.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for sharing a boundary, 1 mark for saying they are next to yours.

24. (3 marks)
   Answer: The farmer grows crops and sells them to the trader. The trader carries the crops to town and sells them. The trader needs the crops and the farmer needs the buyer.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

25. (2 marks)
   Answer: The rain gives the seeds water to grow, and the wet soil is soft to dig.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

26. (5 marks)
   Answer: Shortage of houses: build more houses. Litter: organise cleaning and waste collection. Traffic: improve roads and public transport. Award marks for each problem and each solution.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each problem/solution pair, up to 5 marks.

27. (3 marks)
   Answer: Rain may wash away the soil. Rivers may dry up. There may be landslides or floods.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct result.

28. (2 marks)
   Answer: Say thank you and treat their work with respect. Accept helping them in return.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each way.

29. (5 marks)
   Answer: A polite greeting, the name of the person, the reason for the invitation, the date and time, and a thank-you at the end.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of the five parts.

30. (2 marks)
   Answer: Good rain and fertile soil for farming, and jobs and services in towns. Accept water or good roads.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.
